stories.body: Nvidia shares fell 8.6% in after-hours trading on Wednesday amid reports that its board would consider removing chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang. The company has opened an investigation following allegations of relationships with an employee and a woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence. President Donald Trump has publicly backed Huang, who has advocated easing restrictions on chip exports to China. Analysts warned that replacing him would be difficult because Nvidia's operations and strategy are closely tied to his leadership. The supplied reports did not establish whether the board had reached a decision or identified a successor.
stories.headline: Nvidia board reportedly considers removing Jensen Huang as shares tumble

stories.body: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large prisoner exchange after two days of US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi, but their territorial dispute remained unresolved. US envoy Jared Kushner said the exchange was expected to involve more than 1,000 prisoners from each side; neither government announced a firm total. Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia reported progress on postwar security guarantees, while Russia's delegation reiterated its territorial demands. Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff were due to meet Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday, followed by consultations with Volodymyr Zelensky and European partners in Dublin.
stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree to prisoner exchange as US envoys prepare further talks

stories.body: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei warned that Tehran would target US bases in Europe if they were used to launch attacks on Iran. Israeli media meanwhile reported that the security cabinet had ordered increased military preparations for possible strikes, prompting opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to warn the caretaker government against military action without an immediate threat. Iranian officials also raised the possibility of pre-emptive action if sanctions and the current diplomatic stalemate continued. Washington is maintaining economic pressure, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has argued that its effectiveness makes renewed large-scale military operations unnecessary.
stories.headline: Iran threatens US bases in Europe if they support renewed attacks

stories.body: An Israeli airstrike hit the surgery department at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis early Thursday, killing at least six people and wounding at least 20, according to Gaza's Hamas-run civil defence agency, cited by the BBC. Al Jazeera reported an earlier toll of four at the hospital. The BBC said it could not independently verify the details and had sought an Israeli military response. The attack came as the UN appealed for waterproof tents after heavy rain affected at least 106,000 people, according to UNICEF. UN officials said funding shortages and Israeli restrictions on aid entry were delaying winter supplies.
stories.headline: Gaza civil defence reports at least six killed in strike on Nasser Hospital

stories.body: Around 6,300 schools in Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland received bomb threats, prompting precautionary evacuations at some sites. Italian authorities found no evidence of a concrete danger, while Scottish police assessed the messages as hoaxes and advised that the emails alone did not justify evacuations. Similar wording and a shared purported sender appeared in messages sent to different countries, but authorities had not established whether the incidents were connected or identified those responsible. The threats followed recent bomb hoaxes targeting European airports and other institutions.
stories.headline: Hoax bomb threats disrupt thousands of schools in Italy and the UK

stories.body: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi by fewer than 5,000 votes out of nearly a million counted. The local prosecutor won 49.2% to Hyde-Smith's 48.7%, according to figures cited by the BBC, and she conceded on Wednesday. Colom becomes the first Black person elected to the Senate from Mississippi since Reconstruction and the first Democrat elected to represent the state there in 44 years. His campaign focused on living costs and Hyde-Smith's support for Trump's tariffs. The result brings Democrats to 55 Senate seats, with Alaska still uncalled.
stories.headline: Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat in historic Democratic upset

stories.body: Some congressional Republicans are encouraging Secretary of State Marco Rubio to run for president after the party's midterm losses, arguing that Vice President JD Vance could struggle to escape his association with Trump's unpopular administration. Politico's interviews with roughly two dozen Republican lawmakers found growing interest in alternatives, although Vance retains committed supporters. Rubio has given no indication that he intends to run and continues to defend the Iran war, which could also complicate his prospects. Lawmakers expect other potential contenders, including Ron DeSantis, Josh Hawley and Ted Cruz, to consider bids.
stories.headline: Republican lawmakers urge Marco Rubio to consider a 2028 presidential run

stories.body: The Department of Homeland Security's watchdog will investigate whether ICE officers are complying with body-camera requirements. The Washington Post reports that federal immigration officers involved in several shootings either lacked cameras or did not have them switched on.
stories.headline: DHS watchdog to investigate ICE body-camera compliance

stories.body: The Supreme Court heard arguments over federal agencies' authority to impose fines in the Sun Valley Orchards case. The dispute follows decisions by the court's conservative majority limiting federal regulators' powers, although some conservative justices appeared skeptical of extending those restrictions further, according to The Washington Post.
stories.headline: Supreme Court weighs further limits on federal agencies' power to impose fines

stories.body: A new Gallup poll finds that American support for the death penalty has fallen to its lowest level in 50 years. The decline is most pronounced among Democrats and younger Americans, according to The Washington Post.
stories.headline: US support for the death penalty reaches a 50-year low

stories.body: Spain's attorney general has ordered an investigation into possible offences involving the production, distribution and sale of child sexual abuse material on TikTok, following a complaint from Maldita.es. The organisation reported finding more than 1,000 abusive videos with nearly 48 million views during a 35-day investigation, alongside accounts directing buyers to illegal material. Spain's data protection agency has requested information from TikTok and plans targeted blocking of unlawful content after reviewing the evidence. It says it lacks authority to shut down the entire platform, as the government requested. TikTok says it has acted to remove the material and will cooperate with authorities.
stories.headline: Spanish prosecutors investigate child sexual abuse material on TikTok

stories.body: Messages seized by Spanish police allegedly show members of the neo-Nazi group Núcleo Nacional planning violent attacks on mosques, synagogues and centres for unaccompanied migrant minors. El País reports that the chats form part of an investigation led by a court in Gijón, following 14 arrests last week. The messages identified Muslims, Jews, immigrants, antifascists and vulnerable groups as targets.
stories.headline: Police chats reveal alleged neo-Nazi plans to attack mosques and synagogues

stories.body: Spain's government will challenge provisions in Valencia's budget-related legislation before the Constitutional Court, including rules giving Spaniards priority in access to housing and social benefits. The law was approved in July by the PP and Vox. The government argues that the preference violates basic equality protections and intends to contest around 20 of the law's 200 articles. Other disputed provisions concern family reunification for children in care, restrictions on burqas and niqabs in public spaces, LGBT equality in education and protections for the unborn.
stories.headline: Spanish government to challenge Valencia's national-priority rules

stories.body: Mayor Jaume Collboni said around 50 people were arrested after groups of masked youths damaged shops and burned bins following Wednesday's largely peaceful housing demonstration and general strike. An earlier Mossos d'Esquadra count put arrests at 18. Disturbances affected Passeig de Gràcia, Plaça de Catalunya, Carrer de Pelai and nearby streets, with police using foam projectiles. Collboni said six to ten shops were vandalised and that the city would seek compensation from those convicted. Local reporting said calm had returned by late evening. The wider strike protested housing costs and the gap between wages and living expenses.
stories.headline: Around 50 arrested after unrest follows Barcelona housing demonstration

stories.body: Catalunya activated its Ventcat wind pre-alert as Storm Charles was forecast to bring strong westerly and southwesterly gusts on Thursday after overnight rain. Meteocat warned that gusts could exceed 72 km/h across much of Catalunya, while parts of Barcelona could see more than 60 km/h during the afternoon. Rain was expected to clear early, with winds strongest between midday and late afternoon. Civil protection advised securing objects on balconies and terraces, avoiding trees and unstable structures, and reducing driving speeds. Cooler weather was forecast towards the weekend.
stories.headline: Strong winds forecast across Catalunya after Storm Charles brings overnight rain

stories.body: The Vatican appointed Girona bishop Octavi Vilà to succeed Cardinal Joan Josep Omella as archbishop of Barcelona. Vilà, a Cistercian monk and former abbot of Poblet, has led the Girona diocese since 2024. He previously worked in a newspaper archive and entered monastic life in 2005 after studying history and librarianship. Reports describe him as conciliatory, socially engaged and supportive of Catalan identity. His inaugural ministry celebration is scheduled for 19 December at the Sagrada Família because the cathedral is undergoing works. Omella, now 80, will retire to Zaragoza.
stories.headline: Octavi Vilà appointed archbishop of Barcelona
